2	 * Lakeview Labs & Kidney Care: FOLIO export, version 1.
3	 *
4	 * Lakeview runs an outreach reference laboratory and a nephrology clinic on one system. The export is a
5	 * row-for-row copy of that system's tables. Every payload entry is one table row; its `type` is the table
6	 * name. Column names are the database's own (UPPER_SNAKE). Codes are Lakeview's, documented below; the
7	 * tables at the end of this file list every code value in use.
8	 *
9	 * Two kinds of item, each with its own entry type:
10	 *
11	 * - **Lab report items** (`LabReportRow`): one item per requisition, i.e. one set of specimens drawn at
12	 *   one time for one ordering client. Holds exactly one LAB_REQ row, one LAB_ORDER row per ordered test,
13	 *   and the LAB_RESULT rows those orders produced. Published when every order on the requisition is
14	 *   resulted, cancelled or void (rarely earlier, with 'P' rows, when a slow test holds up a requisition
15	 *   with urgent results). Lab items have no author (system-generated) and no narrative.
16	 * - **Clinic contact items** (`ClinicRow`): one item per nephrology clinic contact (office visit or
17	 *   telephone contact). Holds exactly one CLINIC_VISIT row plus the VISIT_DX, VITAL, MED_ORDER and
18	 *   MED_STATUS_HIST rows entered during that contact. The narrative is the note the nephrologist typed
19	 *   and signed; it is short and is never generated from the rows.
20	 *
21	 * Changes: rows are never edited in place in the export. When a row changes after its item was
22	 * published (a result invalidated, an order marked entered in error), Lakeview publishes a new item that
23	 * `supersedes` the old one and restates every row of the requisition or contact with current values.
24	 * Exception: a medication's status changes are separate MED_STATUS_HIST rows in a later contact, not a
25	 * re-published MED_ORDER row. See MED_ORDER.MED_STATUS.
26	 *
27	 * Times: every timestamp column is RFC 3339 with the UTC offset in effect in America/Chicago at that
28	 * moment (e.g. `2026-02-09T08:14:00-06:00`). Date-only columns are local calendar dates.
29	 *
30	 * Identifiers: REQ_ID, ORDER_ID, RESULT_ID, ACCESSION, VISIT_ID, RX_ID and HIST_ID are Lakeview-assigned,
31	 * never reused, and unique across the whole export (not only within an item). Rows refer to rows in
32	 * other items by these ids.
33	 */

39	/** One row in a lab report item. */

44	  type: 'LAB_REQ';
45	
46	  /** Requisition id, e.g. "RQ-2602090412". */
47	  REQ_ID: string;
48	
49	  /**

51	   * - 'NGFM': Northgate Family Medicine (outside primary care practice).
52	   * - 'LVNEPH': Lakeview's own nephrology clinic.
53	   * Other client codes exist for other patients; CLIENT_NAME always carries the display name.
54	   */
55	  CLIENT_CODE: string;
56	
57	  /** Display name of the ordering client, as on the requisition. */
58	  CLIENT_NAME: string;
59	
60	  /** NPI of the ordering clinician, 10 digits. Absent when the requisition was standing-order only. */
61	  ORDERING_NPI?: string;
62	
63	  /** Ordering clinician's name, "Last, First Credential", as typed on the requisition. */
64	  ORDERING_NAME?: string;
65	
66	  /**

68	   * All specimens on one requisition share it.
69	   */
70	  COLLECTED_AT: string;
71	
72	  /** When the specimens were logged in at the laboratory. */
73	  RECEIVED_AT: string;
74	
75	  /**
76	   * Patient-reported fasting status at draw.
77	   * - 'Y': fasting at least 8 hours.
78	   * - 'N': not fasting.

95	  REQ_ID: string;

104	  /** Display name of the ordered test as printed on the requisition. */

153	
154	  /** Free-text reason entered with status 5 or 9, e.g. "Duplicate order". Absent for other statuses. */

1	/**
2	 * Consumer views: the rows a patient-facing chart application shows for one patient's record at one
3	 * health organization.
4	 *
5	 * Each organization publishes record items ({@link FolioItem}). For each organization a mapper implements
6	 * {@link Transform}: it receives every item that organization published for one patient (in any order,
7	 * including superseded and retracted items) and a local date `asOf` (`YYYY-MM-DD`), and returns
8	 * {@link ViewRows}: the organization's record as it stood at the end of that day. A view the organization has
9	 * nothing for is an empty array.
10	 *
11	 * Rules shared by every view:
12	 *
13	 * - **As-of.** An item counts when its `recorded` time is on or before the end of `asOf` (23:59:59.999 local
14	 *   time). Among those, an item does not count if a counting item supersedes it (directly or through a chain:
15	 *   if C supersedes B and B supersedes A, A is replaced too) or retracts it. A superseding or retracting item
16	 *   recorded after `asOf` has no effect yet. `supersedes` and `retracts` only refer to items of the same issuer.
17	 * - **Corrections versus changes.** Supersession replaces an item entirely (correction, amendment, re-statement).
18	 *   A retracted item was entered in error and is treated as if it never existed. A change in clinical state (a
19	 *   medicine paused, a problem resolved) arrives as a new fact in a new item, not as a supersession; the
20	 *   earlier item still counts as history.
21	 * - **Time zone.** The consumer's time zone is America/Chicago. "Local date" and "local time" mean wall-clock
22	 *   time there. Convert date-times that carry an offset or zone to local time (e.g. `2025-03-04T03:30:00Z` is
23	 *   local date 2025-03-03, 21:30). A date-time with no offset and no zone is already local time: report it as
24	 *   written, never shift it and never drop it. A plain date is a local date.
25	 * - **Partial dates.** A source date may be only a year (`2019`) or a year and month (`2019-06`). Keep exactly
26	 *   the precision the source has; never pad to a full date.
27	 * - **Only what this organization records.** Report what this organization's items say, without inference from
28	 *   other organizations and without correcting the source. Rows come from structured payload entries; the
29	 *   narrative may help interpret an entry, but is never the only basis for a row.
30	 * - **Evidence.** Every row lists the items (and, where the payload has them, entry ids) it rests on; at least
31	 *   the item that gives the row its current state.
32	 * - **Sensitive entries.** Report everything, including entries the organization marks restricted or
33	 *   confidential. Tag rows with `sensitivity` when the source marks the entry with a sensitive category (map
34	 *   the source's own category) or when the entry plainly belongs to one (e.g. quetiapine for bipolar disorder →
35	 *   `mental-health`). Never drop a row because it is sensitive; whether to show or share it is the patient's
36	 *   later decision.
37	 * - **Determinism.** Same input, same output. No clock, randomness, network or file access.
38	 */

I wrote `out/transform.ts`. It type-checks, and `sh in/harness/check.sh 2023-12-31` runs on the sample patient and prints sensible rows. I only looked at the first part of that output (medications, problems, labs and the start of vitals), and I tested no other `asOf` dates or other patients. It never produces allergy rows.

Judgment calls:

- **As-of and replacement.** An item counts if it was recorded before the next local midnight. Retractions only count from items that themselves count. Supersession is followed through chains, even through a retracted link.
- **Labs.**
  - **Left out:** results marked corrected-away (`C`) or not performed (`X`), and results of orders cancelled or entered in error (status 5 or 9). A hemolyzed potassium that is still `F` is kept.
  - **Race-adjusted eGFR:** `LK-EGFR09A` is dropped, so only the non-race and 2021 eGFRs are reported.
  - **Values:** comparators are split out (">90" gives 90 with `>`). Platelet and WBC counts stay in K/uL, which is the target unit.
  - **Equation:** read from the comment text, falling back to the test code.
  - **Collection time:** `COLLECTED_AT` from the requisition.
  - **Duplicates:** copies of the same result are merged, preferring the final one.
- **Problems.**
  - **Grouping and status:** the latest diagnosis per condition counts. All `N18.x` codes are one CKD condition, and other codes group by their 3-character category. `A` is active, `H` is resolved, and `R` and `P` give no row.
  - **CKD categories:** `ckd_stage` and `albuminuria` come from the latest visit that recorded them, falling back to the `N18` code.
  - **Onset:** I take it from "since …" phrases in the narrative text that wraps the diagnosis, which is where the sample's 2015 diabetes and 11/2010 hypertension onsets come from. The payload has no onset field. That is the one place I used the narrative as the basis for a value.
- **Medications.**
  - **Status:** it is the latest status-history row, or the order's own status if there is none. A prescription ever entered in error is dropped.
  - **One row per drug:** the row whose latest event is most recent wins. The ingredient comes from the drug name with the strength and salt words removed.
  - **Dates and reason:** `status_since` is the date of the last status change, or the start date if there was none. The stop reason is mapped from the reason code, and the history comment becomes `status_reason_text`.
  - **Sensitivity:** `mental-health` and `substance-use` are tagged from small drug-name lists.
- **Vitals.** One clinic row per visit. The time is the first blood-pressure time, and a second blood-pressure reading goes in the repeat fields. Weight is rounded to one decimal.
- **Allergies.** I left this view empty. I skipped drug-attributed diagnoses (such as `T36`–`T50` adverse-effect codes) because the reaction details would have been guesses.
